steps.notes: First request in the recording; page_group 'Home'.

Note the dual nature: in this recording the SKU is *derived* from the search response (same value shows up in the search results, the PDP path, and the cart-add body), so it behaves like a correlation value within one session even though it's fundamentally catalog test data. Decide deliberately: (a) parametrize sku directly for a fixed add-to-cart test, or (b) parametrize the search keyword and extract/correlate the SKU from the search response to simulate a real search-then-select journey. As currently written it is a hardcoded literal that keeps working only as long as LAP-2001 stays in the catalog.

correlation_candidates.notes: Replayed verbatim as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' on every subsequent request in the recording (found via response_snippet on the Login entry, then confirmed identical across the Authorization headers of the next 3 requests). This is the single biggest replay-breaking risk in this recording: the literal string 'eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.abcdefg' is a JWT and will expire. Hardcoding it means the script works once and then returns 401s on every request after Login on every subsequent run or iteration.

consumed_by: Not explicitly re-sent as a request Cookie header anywhere in this HAR (browser's automatic cookie jar handled it) — must be captured and replayed explicitly by a load-testing tool.
correlation_candidates.notes: Found via response_set_cookie on the Login entry: 'SESSIONID=a1b2c3d4e5f6; Path=/; HttpOnly'. HttpOnly cookie set at login. Because the HAR was captured from a real browser, the browser resent this cookie automatically on later requests without it ever showing up explicitly as a request header in the capture — a load-testing tool will not do this automatically, so it must be extracted and replayed as a Cookie header on every subsequent call or server-side session state may not match what the bearer token implies.

consumed_by: None observed — the recording ends at Add to Cart.

No consumer is observed in this recording, but this is the classic ID that any Checkout / Place Order step layered on top of this flow would need — must not be hardcoded if the journey is extended.

Found via response_snippet on the Login entry (value 98213). Captured by the server at login but never reused anywhere in this recording — flagged as captured-but-unused; may be needed by account/order flows not present in this capture.

risk_flags: No logout / session-end step: the recording stops immediately after Add to Cart, mid-session — checkout, place-order, and logout behavior are all unverified.

The JWT bearer token from Login and the SESSIONID session cookie are both correlation candidates that are easy to miss: the JWT appears as a literal Authorization header value on 3 later requests in the raw HAR, and if copied as-is into a script it will work for exactly one run, then fail with 401s on every iteration after the token expires.

The SESSIONID cookie is never shown being resent as a request header in this HAR because the capture is browser-based (automatic cookie jar) — a replay tool must extract it from Set-Cookie and add it explicitly, or session state may not match what the bearer token implies.

Only one session / one journey was recorded (no thread groups or scenarios in a HAR) — no data to infer relative task weighting (e.g. browse-only vs. login-and-buy users), and only one example each of username, password, search keyword, SKU, and quantity, all needing more variety before load testing.

cartId and customerId are both captured by the server but never consumed later in this recording — can't confirm from this capture alone how a checkout step would use them; revisit when the flow is extended past Add to Cart.

A 302 redirect from /old-home to '/' appears mid-session. It reads as a trivial legacy-URL bounce (same host, lands back on the already-visited home page) rather than an SSO/auth hop, but it was deliberately kept (not filtered as noise) and is called out here rather than silently folded away.

Platform detected as Generic (no Magento/SFCC/Mirakl/Shopify signal) — this looks like a custom/headless REST + JWT storefront ('/api/login', '/api/cart/add'), so platform-specific correlation conventions (form_key, quoteId, dwsid) don't apply; only the generic bearer-token + cookie pattern does.

Recording is short (6 business requests, ~12 seconds, a single session) — token/session lifetime can't be observed directly from one capture; the expiry risk on the JWT is inferred from its format, not confirmed by watching it fail.
